glyph_origin: Pictogram (象形) – originally depicting a sacred composite creature in ancient China, combining features of the snake, crocodile, fish, deer, etc. Shang oracle-bone and bronze forms usually show a large-mouthed beast head and an S-shaped geometric body; Shang bronzes and decorative motifs show diamond- or scale-like patterning associated with snakes (perhaps fish or crocodile scales), occasionally with legs. In oracle-bone forms, the head bears one or two inverted 王-shaped elements (i.e. inverted axe/halberd forms) or a 玉-like ornament. The form in Heji H04655 matches Shang bronze forms, which are more pictorial, like an inverted axe/halberd attached above the head; scholars generally derive this “bottle-shaped horn” from deer antlers, though some bronze forms instead attach a bell-shaped or shell-like undeciphered graph or clan emblem. In Western Zhou bronzes, the head ornament tends toward 辛; by the late Western Zhou and early Spring and Autumn period, the mouth is drawn downward into 肉, and the body behind the head develops a large bulge, like a snake swollen after swallowing a large animal. Thereafter head and body separate into the left and right parts of the character; …
s_page_origin: Simplified from 𢅛, a variant form of 龍. 帝 is then removed, leaving out 尨. This was simplified even further by removing two of the three strokes of 彡. see 龍
note: glyph_origin is from the traditional page 龍; s_page_origin explains the simplified 龙.
